name: unicorn
why: A CPU emulation framework that lets you run machine code for many architectures in isolation, a great way to watch programs execute.

brief.what_it_is: Unicorn is a CPU emulator framework, a library rather than a standalone app. You hand it machine code for a supported architecture (ARM, ARM64, M68K, MIPS, PowerPC, RISC-V, SPARC, S390X, TriCore, or x86 in 16/32/64-bit) plus memory and register state, and it executes that code in an emulated CPU. Hooks let you observe execution at fine-grained levels. The README says it is written in C with bindings for many languages, including Python, Rust, Go, Ruby, Java, and Lua.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a lightweight, architecture-neutral emulator for running code in isolation, with a clean API across many CPU families. The homepage says it was introduced at BlackHat USA 2015 as a cross-architecture CPU emulation framework and became a foundation for security research.
brief.how_it_works: Unicorn is based on QEMU, but it is a rewritten, library-only core with an architecture-neutral API. It uses just-in-time compilation for performance. Instrumentation hooks let callers inspect execution at various levels.
brief.install_notes: The README points to docs/COMPILE.md for building and installing from source and to docs/README.md for more documentation. The homepage says precompiled binaries are available in its Download section. The GitHub badges reference PyPI downloads, which suggests a Python package exists, but I did not confirm an install command. Building from source was not covered in what I fetched.
brief.standout: Its pitch is one API across many CPU architectures, not one emulator per CPU. It is also a library you embed, so you drive execution from your own code and use hooks to watch it, rather than running a binary.
brief.status: Unknown, with mixed signals. The homepage's most recent news items are dated November 2022, including release 2.0.1 on November 1, 2022 and an award on November 13, 2022. The GitHub README carries a banner reading "LOOKING FOR CONTRIBUTORS!" and has fuzzing and downloads badges. I did not check commit history or release dates on GitHub.
brief.caveats: The README says the project is GPLv2, which matters if you plan to embed it in closed-source work. The README lists confirmed platforms as Windows and *nix, with macOS, Linux, Android, BSD, and Solaris confirmed; I did not check build pain on any of them. The homepage's Unicorn2 news says the 2.x line was built from scratch on QEMU 5 and that bindings were updated afterward. Its page says the 2.0.1 release fixed many issues in v2.0, so earlier 2.0 builds may be buggy. The project is asking for contributors.
quotes: Unicorn is a lightweight, multi-platform, multi-architecture CPU emulator framework, based on QEMU.
Unicorn is based on QEMU, but it goes much further with a lot more to offer.
